topics.parent_demand: Category head demand 'dash cam' plus the US autocomplete seed '4 channel dash cam' (Q09); buyers shop a shortlist before any brand is settled.
topics.business_question: When a US buyer asks for dash cams with no scenario attached, which brands does AI list, and does the brand enter that list?
topics.possible_action: Category-level content and third-party evidence; the conditioned rows point to the proof pages the brand is missing (night footage, sensor, warranty terms).
topics.note: Kept deliberately light (5 Prompts) because the P1 Attributes sit in the parking and coverage scenarios; the single no-condition Prompt is the category baseline instrument.

topics.parent_demand: US autocomplete seeds 'dash cam parking mode', 'dash cam parking mode without hardwire', 'dash cam parking mode drain battery' (Q10, Q11) plus the r/Dashcam parking threads (Q01, Q02).
topics.business_question: For buyers who park on the street or in a lot, does AI treat Bbrand as a real parking-monitoring option, or does the hardwire/accessory requirement knock it out?
topics.possible_action: Rewrite the parking-mode block on the product page so trigger, runtime and hardwire requirement agree, and state what is in the box; this is the P1 evidence gap.
topics.note: Carries both P1 Attributes. The product-page FAQ already contradicts the first-screen 24/7 claim, which is why changeability is high here.

topics.parent_demand: US autocomplete seed '4 channel dash cam' (Q09) and the buyer language 'maximum exterior coverage' (Q03); the category's multi-channel sub-demand.
topics.business_question: Where buyers want more than a front camera, does AI name Bbrand for four-way coverage, and is the coverage claim legible as evidence rather than a spec line?
topics.possible_action: Publish comparison-ready coverage proof (which camera records what, at what resolution) and a clip-retrieval walkthrough.
topics.note: Holds the coverage attribute where the H1 front 3K beats the collected multi-channel pages; weight sits here because it is the brand's clearest spec advantage.

attribute_plan.reason: Q10 and Q11 are direct problem questions (parking mode without hardwire; battery drain) and Q02 asks what else must be bought. Category norm is parity — RivalB3 states parking mode needs a separately sold hardwire kit, and Bbrand sells a fuse-tap kit too — yet Bbrand buries the requirement in the product FAQ under a first-screen '24/7 Parking Protection' claim. Capability exists and the category is level, so this is an evidence gap one page closes: 高 changeability.

Q01 asks for continuous parked recording, not collision-only. The collected RivalB3 N5 page publishes buffered motion detection (10 s pre-roll + 30 s after), adjustable motion zones and two continuous low-bitrate modes, while the Bbrand page describes only a 1-minute collision clip plus 1 fps time-lapse up to 24 h — and its own FAQ contradicts the first-screen 24/7 claim. Position trails on trigger richness; whether the capability itself is absent is unconfirmed, so it stays 中 rather than 低.

Maximum exterior coverage is the buyer's stated goal (Q03) and the brand's clearest spec lead: H1 front 3K + rear/left/right 1080P versus RivalB3 N5 front 2.7K and RivalB4 VisionPano 40 front 2.5K (official pages, Internet Archive snapshots). The claim is already published, so the remaining work is third-party reinforcement, not a page gap: 中.

attribute_plan.settle_with: Brand material: night-vision sensor model and sample night footage showing a readable plate; the Bbrand page only says 'Enhanced Low-Light Capture'.
attribute_plan.reason: Reading a plate at night is the decisive evidence criterion for this audience (Q04) and buyers raise it directly. The comparison cannot be settled publicly because the brand publishes no sensor or night sample; both competitor pages lead with STARVIS 2 and plate capture. Held at 中, not downgraded by default.

Buyers use STARVIS 2 as a proxy for night quality (Q05), and both collected competitor titles state the sensor while the Bbrand page states none. Publishing the sensor is a separate action from proving night output, so it stays its own row. Whether the H1 actually carries a comparable sensor is unconfirmed — treat as evidence gap first, capability gap only if the brand says so.

A hot car in summer is the failure buyers fear (Q07: battery swelling). Bbrand publishes a supercapacitor rated -20 °C to 70 °C and RivalB3 markets a supercapacitor for the same reason, so the category is level and the fact is already published — reinforcement work, not a page gap.

The Case names after-sales confidence as a purchase barrier and Q08/Q12 show buyers checking service and warranty before buying. On the collected pages RivalB4 offers 24 months (2 years plus a 6-month extension) and a 30-day money-back guarantee, while Bbrand advertises 1 year; the Bbrand warranty page terms were not collected. Trails on the published term, but clearer terms and returns content can still move what AI says, so 中.

Budget is an explicit buyer constraint ($200 in Q08, $100 in Q04). On the collected snapshots the H1 4-camera lists at $209 against $299.99 for the RivalB4 VisionPano 40 and $379.99 for the RivalB3 N5, so the entry price leads — but price is a copyable, fast-moving claim, so it is graded for parity and kept experimental.

Q06 puts rear camera quality and the night screen on the pre-price checklist, and a four-camera product is only as good as its weakest channel. Rear/side resolution is 1080P class on the collected N5 and VisionPano 40 pages as well, so parity with published specs: 中.

Q06 lists SD-card support as a pre-purchase check and the clip has to be findable after an incident. Capacity and app retrieval are published (128 GB included, 512 GB max, 5.8 GHz Wi-Fi); the RivalB3 N5 page goes to 1 TB, so capacity is parity-to-behind rather than a lead.

The buyer job behind Q01 is catching damage when nobody is around, and every multi-channel model in the collected set offers a parked-impact mode. Capability is at parity and described on the page, so improvement rides on the parking-mode block rather than a separate asset: 中.
Only Case-level language about install convenience; no buyer quote in this pass raises the mount itself, and the wiring half of installation is measured under Parking Power & Hardwire Setup.
attribute_plan.no_carrier_reason: No buyer quote raises mount difficulty; the wiring half of installation is already measured under Parking Power & Hardwire Setup, so a separate Prompt would duplicate that decision.

attribute_plan.reason: Q06 lists how annoying the screen is at night, but only as one item among six checks and with no sign it removes a candidate.
attribute_plan.no_carrier_reason: One checklist mention only (Q06); no evidence it changes the candidate set, so it stays visible at P3 with no Prompt.

competitor_selection.note: The Case's three competitors are frozen and are not re-verified here; no Competitor Prompts exist at the discovery stage, so they appear in no Prompt wording.

collection_config.platform_note: The presales answer batch ran four platforms but the platform list is not part of the inputs; fix it with the client before the candidate baseline.
collection_config.cadence: 5 candidate-baseline runs per Prompt per platform; core Discovery then weekly as agreed, experimental Prompts on a trigger.

parked.item: How do I install a fuse-tap hardwire kit myself?
parked.reason: How-to question: AI returns instructions, not a candidate list, so it does not fit the Discovery contract. The buying decision behind it is carried by BOT-US-T2-D02/D04.

parked.item: Is it legal to record audio inside my car in my state?
parked.reason: Pure legal knowledge; the next step belongs to a state statute, not to the brand's product. No Information Prompt without buyer-demand evidence in this batch.

parked.item: What is the difference between 2K and 4K dash cams?
parked.reason: Education question with no candidate ask; the category-understanding value is already captured by the night and sensor Prompts in T1.
